member.name: T:BulkutMobile.AndroidFfmpegRunner
member.summary: FFmpeg on Android. The platform forbids starting an executable from an app sandbox, so the native FFmpegKit library is linked instead and every command runs in process. Its output becomes plain log lines, which is exactly what the probe and the silence analysis already consume on desktop.

member.name: M:BulkutMobile.AndroidFfmpegRunner.PrepareAsync(System.IProgress{Bulkut.Core.Services.EngineStatus},System.Threading.CancellationToken)
member.summary: Loads the native library once at startup by asking for its banner, so a device that cannot run FFmpeg shows an engine error instead of failing on the first render.

member.name: M:BulkutMobile.AndroidFfmpegRunner.ExecuteAsync(System.Collections.Generic.IReadOnlyList{System.String},System.Double,System.IProgress{Bulkut.Core.Models.RenderProgress},System.Threading.CancellationToken)
member.summary: FFmpegKit does expensive work on the calling thread — loading the native library, building the session — so a command is never started from the UI thread. On a cold start that load takes seconds even on a fast device.

member.name: M:BulkutMobile.AndroidFfmpegRunner.ReadTranscript(Ffmpegkit.Droid.AbstractSession,System.Collections.Generic.List{System.String})
member.summary: The complete FFmpeg transcript, one line per entry. The session output is preferred because individual log entries arrive in chunks; the buffered and live copies are only fallbacks.

member.name: T:BulkutMobile.AndroidPlatform
member.summary: Android has no home folder to write to. Renders land in the app's external files folder, which every file manager can see under Android/data, and the share sheet is offered as the "reveal" action.
